To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sarcoidosis is characterized by a unique high‐level ICOS phenotype of Tregs in the inflamed lung.

Pulmonary sarcoidosis, a granulomatosis of unknown aetio­logy, is associated with high ICOS expression on lung CD4+CD25+Foxp3+ regulatory T cells (lung Tregs) and lung CD4+ effector T cells (lung effector T cells).
sarcoidosis‐associated lung CD4+ CD25+ FoxP3+ regulatory T cells (lung Tregs) express high‐level inducer co‐stimulator protein (ICOS), whereas blood Tregs and lung effector T cell subsets do not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel biomarkers for disease course and resolution of pulmonary sarcoidosis.
the identification of novel immune‐modulatory pathways in sarcoidosis.
the identification of new biomarkers for the prognosis of disease activity and resolution in sarcoidosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ICOS expression on regulatory T cells and monocyte ICOS‐L are potential markers for the prognosis of acute sarcoidosis.
ICOS expression in Tregs and ICOS‐L expression in non‐classical CD14lowCD16+ monocytes is a hallmark of pulmonary sarcoidosis, which is particularly prominent in LS patients.
ICOS is a promising biomarker for the disease activity and resolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ICOS‐ICOS‐L axis is a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of sarcoidosis and other inflammatory lung diseases.
ICOS expression is restricted to lung Tregs in sarcoidosis and that ICOS‐L expression on blood monocytes is increased in LS.
the ICOS‐high phenotype of lung Tregs is a unique feature in sarcoidosis, particularly in patients with acute disease, which may contribute to the resolution of disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ICOS is expressed in a unique manner on lung regulatory T cell subsets in patients with pulmonary sarcoidosis.
the inducible costimulator (ICOS) is a potential biomarker for the course of pulmonary sarcoidosis and its resolution.
the ICOS pathway is involved in the pathogenesis and resolution of lung inflammation in sarcoidosis.
